title: High-throughput and cost effective pan trap DNA extraction
author: Jordan P Cuff
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b2csqawe
materials: Wash Buffer 1 should be comprised of the following reagents: A B C D 1 Reagent Required concentration in buffer Chemical molarity Amount per 100 mL 2 Guanidine HCl 7 M 95.53 29.4 g 3 Ethanol 56 % - 56 mL 4 H2O - - 44 mL

steps.title: Set and fill pan traps
steps.instruction: Clean each pan trap with Chemgene or diluted bleach, place at vegetation height, fill with 30 mL detergent‑water solution, leave in the field for 72 h, then retrieve.

steps.title: Collect and store trap contents
steps.instruction: Pour trap liquid through a sterilised funnel into a labelled container, transport on ice and store at –20 °C until processing.

steps.title: Wash specimens in mesh
steps.instruction: Rinse specimens in a fine‑mesh sieve with clean water and transfer to a 50 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer 1
steps.instruction: Make 100 mL Lysis Buffer 1 (pH 9) containing 0.701 g NaCl (120 mM), 5 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl (50 mM), 4 mL 0.5 M EDTA (20 mM) and 91 mL water.

steps.title: Add Lysis Buffer 1
steps.instruction: Add 30 mL of freshly prepared Lysis Buffer 1 to each sample tube so that specimens are fully covered.

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer 2
steps.instruction: Make 100 mL Lysis Buffer 2 (pH 9) with 0.701 g NaCl (120 mM), 5 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl (50 mM), 4 mL 0.5 M EDTA (20 mM), 3 g SDS (3 %), and 91 mL water.

steps.title: Prepare Proteinase Buffer master mix
steps.instruction: For each 96‑well plate combine 51.2 mL Lysis Buffer 2 with 1 584 µL Proteinase K (10 mg mL⁻¹). (Alternative: 102.4 mL Lysis Buffer 2 with 3.168 mL Proteinase K.)

steps.title: Add Proteinase Buffer
steps.instruction: Add 15 mL of the Proteinase Buffer master mix to each tube (or 15 mL of papain master mix – see optional step). Vortex to mix.

steps.title: Add carbon steel beads
steps.instruction: Add three 3 mm hardened carbon‑steel beads to each tube; bake beads for ≥12 h at 250 °C beforehand to remove oil.

steps.title: Grind samples
steps.instruction: Grind the tubes in a Geno/Grinder 2010 at 1 750 RPM for 4 min (2 min for the papain protocol). Repeat if homogenisation is incomplete.

steps.title: Vortex and incubate overnight
steps.instruction: Vortex each tube, then incubate at 37 °C for 12–16 h (overnight) to inactivate proteins.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 4 000 × g for 4 min (or 2 min in some variants).

steps.title: Transfer supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer 1 mL of supernatant to a clean 2.2 mL deep‑well 96‑well plate for archiving; transfer 200 µL to a second deep‑well plate for DNA extraction; store remaining lysate at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Protein Denaturation Buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 47.7 g Guanidine HCl (5 M) in water to a final volume of 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare denaturation master mix
steps.instruction: Per 96‑well plate mix 21.1 mL Protein Denaturation Buffer with 21.1 mL 100 % ethanol (220 µL of each per well).

steps.title: Add denaturation master mix
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL of the master mix to each well containing the 200 µL supernatant; vortex briefly.

steps.title: Load sample onto spin column
steps.instruction: Add ~600 µL of each well’s mixture to a well of a 96‑well silica‑membrane spin‑column plate, cover with a breathable seal and place the plate over a suitable reservoir (e.g., a 2.2 mL deep‑well plate).

steps.title: Bind DNA by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at ≥6 000 × g for 10 min (if the rotor cannot reach 6 000 × g, extend the spin accordingly). Discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash with Buffer 1
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Wash Buffer 1 to each column, cover, centrifuge at ≥6 000 × g for 5 min (or 1 min if speed is higher), discard flow‑through.

steps.title: Prepare Wash Buffer 2
steps.instruction: Make 100 mL Wash Buffer 2 (pH ≈ 7) containing 70 mL 100 % ethanol (70 % v/v), 1 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl (10 mM) and 29 mL water.

steps.title: Wash with Buffer 2
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Wash Buffer 2 to each column, cover, centrifuge at ≥6 000 × g for 15 min (or at 20 000 × g for 3 min). Discard flow‑through.

steps.title: Transfer column to elution plate
steps.instruction: Move the spin‑column plate carefully onto a new 0.5 mL DNA collection plate, avoiding contact of residual ethanol with the membrane.

steps.title: Prepare Elution Buffer
steps.instruction: Make 100 mL Elution Buffer (pH ≈ 7) with 1 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl (10 mM) and 99 mL water.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL Elution Buffer directly onto the silica membrane, incubate at room temperature for 5 min (sealed), then centrifuge at ≥6 000 × g for 2 min. Collect the eluate; it contains purified DNA.

steps.title: Optional repeat elution
steps.instruction: If higher total DNA yield is desired (at the cost of lower concentration), repeat the elution step (add another 200 µL Elution Buffer and centrifuge).

steps.title: Papain‑based alternative (optional)
steps.instruction: Replace Proteinase K with papain: prepare a master mix of 14.54 mL Lysis Buffer 2 and 460 µL papain (100 mg mL⁻¹) per 96‑well plate; add 15 mL of this mix to each sample, grind for 2 min, and continue with the same downstream steps.
